title: Distinguished presentations of reduced affinoids over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial rank-one absolute value, and put $V=\{a\in K:|a|\leq1\}$, its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring]. A Tate algebra $K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_s\rangle$ consists of power series whose coefficients tend to zero, with the Gauss norm; $V\langle U_1,\ldots,U_s\rangle$ is its subring of series with coefficients in $V$. Let $C\ne0$ be a reduced quotient of a Tate algebra, endowed with its affinoid Banach topology. Define $C^\circ=\{c\in C:\{c^m:m\geq0\}\text{ is bounded}\}$. There exist an integer $s\geq0$ and a continuous surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism $q:K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_s\rangle\to C$ whose restriction maps $V\langle U_1,\ldots,U_s\rangle$ onto $C^\circ$.

source.place: Theorem 6.4.3/1 (distinguished presentations), with 6.4.3/6; confirmed by Rodriguez Vazquez, Non-Archimedean normal families, section 2.2, printed p. 1685 (the paragraph preceding Proposition 2.2 and its norm-preserving lifts). Both archival PDFs WANTED.

proof.text: Choose the quotient norm $\|\cdot\|_0$ of an original presentation $q_0:T_r\twoheadrightarrow C$. Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-spectral-banach-norm] to obtain the complete power-multiplicative norm $\rho$ and $\rho\le\|\cdot\|_0\le M\rho$. These inequalities show that a family is bounded for one norm exactly when it is bounded for the other. Consequently $c\in C^\circ$ iff $\rho(c)\le1$: in the forward direction $\rho(c)^m=\rho(c^m)$ is bounded for $m\ge1$, which forces $\rho(c)\le1$; in the reverse direction $\|c^m\|_0\le M$ for $m\ge1$, and the extra power $c^0=1$ is bounded too. Thus the desired target of the restriction is precisely $C_{\le1}$.

source.place: BGR Theorem 6.2.4/1; power-boundedness versus the spectral unit ball, as in Conrad Theorem 1.2.6 and the following paragraph (PDF pp.6–7). Agent assembly, not a transcription of the unavailable BGR proof. Archival copy WANTED; not present in this checkout.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-affinoid-canonical-reduction-finite-type] to choose $b_1,\ldots,b_t\in C_{\le1}$ whose classes generate $\widetilde C$ over $\kappa=V/\mathfrak m$. Keep the original generators $a_i=q_0(X_i)$ as well. By the quotient-norm definition, $\|a_i\|_0\le\|X_i\|_G=1$, so step 1 gives $\rho(a_i)\le1$. Both finite lists therefore lie in the closed unit ball for the complete norm $\rho$. Do not replace the original generators by smaller scalar multiples: such a replacement need not generate $C$ by restricted series.

source.place: BGR sections 6.3–6.4, finite generation of the canonical reduction; adjoining representatives to a fixed affinoid generating set. Agent assembly. Archival copy WANTED; not present in this checkout.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-tate-banach-substitution] to the complete $K$-algebra $(C,\rho)$ and the tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_t)$. The norm, scalar and completeness hypotheses are supplied by step 1; the coordinate bounds are step 2. This produces a continuous $K$-algebra map $q:T_{r+t}\to C$ with $\rho(q(f))\le\|f\|_G$. The coefficient inclusion $\iota:T_r\to T_{r+t}$, adding zero exponents in the last $t$ variables, is an isometric algebra map by the coefficient formulas and [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion]. The maps $q\iota$ and $q_0$ are continuous and agree on constants and the $r$ variables. Uniqueness in the substitution lemma gives $q\iota=q_0$; here $q_0$ is continuous for $\rho$ by step 1. Since $q_0$ is onto, $q$ is onto.

source.place: Conrad Exercise 1.2.8(3), PDF p.7: restricted-series substitution. Retain the old variables so surjectivity follows from the original presentation. Agent assembly. Archival copy WANTED; not present in this checkout.

proof.text: Consider the reduction map $\kappa[U_1,\ldots,U_{r+t}]\to\widetilde C$ induced by this particular $q$. Every class of $\widetilde C$ is a polynomial in the classes of $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ by step 2, so it is the image of a polynomial in the last $t$ variables; hence this reduction map is surjective. Apply [lem-trf-tate-reduction-norm-lifting]. Its base is the given algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued $K$; $C$ is nonzero and reduced; step 3 supplies the continuous surjective contractive map and the preceding sentence supplies its reduction hypothesis. If $c\in C^\circ$, step 1 gives $\rho(c)\le1$, and the lifting lemma gives $f$ with $q(f)=c$ and $\|f\|_G=\rho(c)\le1$. Every coefficient of $f$ is then in $V$, so $f\in V\langle U\rangle$. Conversely, for $f\in V\langle U\rangle$, the Gauss norm is at most one and step 3 gives $\rho(q(f))\le1$; step 1 yields $q(f)\in C^\circ$. Thus $q(V\langle U\rangle)=C^\circ$, with $s=r+t$.

lean.statement: theorem affinoid_distinguished_presentation (K : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] [IsAlgClosed K] (V : ValuationSubring K) (hV : ∀ a : K, a ∈ V ↔ ‖a‖ ≤ 1) (C : Type v) [NormedCommRing C] [CompleteSpace C] [Nontrivial C] [IsReduced C] [Algebra K C] (haff : ∃ (r : ℕ) (q₀ : (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))) →+* C), Function.Surjective q₀ ∧ q₀.comp (constants K r) = algebraMap K C ∧ ∀ U : Set C, IsOpen U ↔ ∀ f, q₀ f ∈ U → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ g, MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm : K → ℝ) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ 1) (g.val - f.val) < ε → q₀ g ∈ U) : ∃ (s : ℕ) (q : (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin s ↦ (1 : ℝ))) →+* C), Function.Surjective q ∧ q.comp (constants K s) = algebraMap K C ∧ (∀ f, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ g, MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm : K → ℝ) (fun _ : Fin s ↦ 1) (g.val - f.val) < δ → ‖q g - q f‖ < ε) ∧ ∀ c : C, (∃ f, (∀ ν : Fin s →₀ ℕ, MvPowerSeries.coeff ν f.val ∈ V) ∧ q f = c) ↔ ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ m : ℕ, ‖c ^ m‖ ≤ M
